questions.question: In your own words, describe the difference between the warm front and the cold front during the Mature Stage of a mid-latitude cyclone.
questions.expected_answer: The cold front is heavy, fast-moving cold air that bulldozes under the warm air, forcing it up quickly and causing heavy rain and thunderstorms. The warm front is light, slower-moving warm air that gently slides up over the back of the cold air, causing steady, gentle rain.

questions.question: Explain why the mid-latitude cyclone 'dies' during the Occluded Stage.
questions.expected_answer: During occlusion, the faster cold front catches up to the slower warm front and completely lifts all the warm air off the ground. Since the warm air is the 'fuel' or energy source for the storm, lifting it away causes the storm to lose power and die out.

questions.question: Why does the Western Cape only experience the effects of mid-latitude cyclones during winter?
questions.expected_answer: In summer, the high-pressure belts shift south and block the cyclones, keeping them out over the ocean. In winter, the pressure belts shift north, opening a path for the westerly winds to steer the cyclones towards the south-western tip of Africa, hitting the Western Cape.
